topic: Reader 2 — JevCode today as the substrate for a parent-child (spawn / sub-agent) model: what exists at main ec61170 and in the locked in-flight worktrees, what docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §3–§7/§12.0 specifies, what a parent-child model can reuse, and what is missing (budget splitting, child identity, merge of child worktrees, cascade of pause/end, TUI events).
facts: [REUSE] Engine interface (src/core/types.ts:1450-1475): readonly runId, events (EngineEmitter on/onAny/emit), signal (the one run-level AbortSignal every generate/ask/sandbox/confirm receives), run() (never rejects; RunResult is the only thing bench and CLI read), abort(reason 'human_abort'|'signal'|'error', {signal?, error?}), status(), snapshotState(), steer(text) (<= 8 x 600, SteerResult ok|empty|full|finished), unsteer(), pause() (void, at-step only), retryNow(), annotate(). No end(), deliver(), resume(), or pause(opts) at main.

[REUSE] Many engines already coexist in one process: src/bench/runner.ts:378-716 keeps `active: Set<Engine>` (:419), one shared AbortController whose abort fans `e.abort('signal')` to every active engine (:431-433), a bench-cap check on every `status` event that aborts siblings with `e.abort('human_abort')` and marks them in `capAborted` so their record reads spend_cap (:421-429, :617-621, :663-675), N concurrent workers pulling units (:697-713, `Promise.all(Array.from({length: min(concurrency, units.length)}, worker))`), and a serialised append chain to tasks.jsonl per finished record for crash safety (:441-447). Engines get `session: { sessionId: null, parentRunId: null, source: 'bench' }` (src/bench/conditions.ts:251).

[REUSE] SpendMeter tree is the in-process budget-splitting primitive (src/core/types.ts:731-743; src/spend/meter.ts:45-128): `child(capUsd)` creates a meter that forwards every add() to its parent (:97-105), `exceeded()` = own total >= cap OR parent.exceeded() (:62-64), `restore()` restores only this meter (never re-adds to the parent, :106-111), root `setCap()` swaps the cap without recreating children (:116-118); bookkeeping never throws. Used today bench->run (`root.child(opts.taskSpendCapUsd)`, runner.ts:581) and session->run via `SessionClamp` (src/cli/session.ts:2349; types.ts:1150-1155; `budget:clamp` event emitted after run:ready, engine.ts:1064).

[REUSE] Parent->child data flow for follow-ups exists: `EngineSeed { parentRunId, plan, window, createdThisRun, lastTestRun, undoLog?, pinnedFiles?, carriedDirectives? }` (types.ts:1131-1146, built by src/session/seed.ts, chosen by cli/session.ts:1912-1933 seedFor), `SessionRef { sessionId, parentRunId, source, title?, clamp?, intake? }` (types.ts:1150-1159), `run:ready` carries sessionId/parentRunId (engine.ts:1045-1056), `RunMeta.sessionId/parentRunId/source` (engine.ts:3207-3211), index `run:start` carries parentRunId (src/session/index.ts:25) and the fold copies it onto RunRow (:322-335). BUT `parentRunId` today means 'follow-up seeded from this earlier run of the SAME session', not a concurrent child; `parentSessionId` appears nowhere in src (grep).

[REUSE] Run identity and locks: RUN_ID_RE `^\d{8}-\d{6}-[a-z2-7]{8}$` (engine.ts:214); createRunDir allocates with non-recursive mkdir and regenerates on EEXIST so concurrent workers never share a dir (engine.ts:3078-3093, DESIGN §9); `run.lock {pid, startedAt, host}` taken O_EXCL with same-host pid liveness (src/session/lock.ts:27-35 isPidAlive, :57-59 lockIsLive, :91-126 acquireRunLock), taken at createEngine for resume (:3152) and fresh (:3217), released in finish() and the 'exit' handler (:923-927); a dead pid or ANOTHER HOST is replaced silently with a warning (lock.ts:117-125) — the hole §3.4 closes with `peerLive`. Workspace realpath is bound at createEngine (:3134): relocation is always stop + resume, never an in-process rebind.

[REUSE] Cancellation plumbing: one `controller` per engine (engine.ts:486, signal assigned :653) handed to decider (:1611), synthesis (:1802), generator (:1931), confirmer (:2532) and every retry sleep; per-sample linked aborts `linkSample()` via `linkedAbort` (:2042-2055) so a sample deadline or loser-cancellation aborts one sample without failing the stage; per-sample retry wakers `sampleWakers` woken by retryNow() (:976-990); `awaitBlocker` races abort / human answer / jev-unreachable auto-retry timer (:1189-1230; no blocker => 'stop' at once for bench, --plain pipe, --no-input, --json); abort() kills the sandbox tree (`sandbox.killAll()`, :883) and installs a process 'exit' handler that writes state synchronously and releases the lock (:884-897); second abort => `forceExit` = writeStateSync + process.exit (:910-921).

[REUSE] Pause today: `pause()` sets `pauseRequested`, emits `pause:requested {step}`, and is consumed ONLY at the loop top after the in-flight step committed whole (engine.ts:965-969, :1106) => `finish('human_pause')`, exit 4, resumable without --force (src/loop/stop.ts:9; types.ts:310). `EngineStatus.pausing` = pauseRequested && lastResult === null (:837). Idempotent; no-op once finish() began (`isFinished()`, :775).

[REUSE] Checkpoint/resume mechanics: checkpoint N overlaps step N+1 up to `await this.pendingCheckpoint` before anything touches the workspace (engine.ts:2310), then the blocked discard (:2311-2317), `checkBudgets(['spend_cap','wall_time'])` (:2318), `takePreImages` (:2328), execute (:2330), post-images (:2339), judge (:2347) — the exact seam where §4.2 inserts the `coordinate` micro-stage. Rule-1 discards keep `state.interrupted = {step, stage, proposal}`; `markLastResort` writes it on 'exit' (:903-908). finish() awaits the pending checkpoint, writes final state, then `Promise.allSettled(pendingPersists)` inside a 5 s `SHUTDOWN_CHECKPOINT_BOUND_MS` (:217, :2952-3040) and forceExits on timeout. Resume gates in createEngine: state.runId match, mode match, `complete` needs --force, live lock refuses (:3143-3152). DESIGN §9: resume always starts a fresh step at intent; no recorded proposal is replayed (deliberately deviated by COORDINATION §7.3 step 3 under a hash gate).

[REUSE] Worktree lanes (src/synth/sieve/lanes.ts) are the isolation recipe: `LaneContext = { runDir, sandbox: Pick<Sandbox,'run'>, signal, workspaceInfo }` (:55-60); `createLanes(ctx, oracle, {count, workspaceBytes})` picks candidate_file | worktree | copy | inplace (:183-188), worktree mode runs `rm -rf <dir> && git worktree prune` then `git worktree add --detach <runDir>/tmp/synth/lane<k> HEAD` (:213-214) and replays the dirty set (tracked+untracked, `DIRTY_ENTRIES_MAX` 200, :45, :161-181); `withLane` is a FIFO acquire -> fn -> resetLane (`git checkout -- . && git clean -fdq`, :260) -> release (:279-306); `disposeLanes` = `git worktree remove --force` falling back to `rm -rf && git worktree prune` (:308-327); all shell goes through `ctx.sandbox.run(cmd, {cwd, signal: ctx.signal, timeoutMs 120 s})` (:90). Lanes write only under laneDir (seatbelt writable roots: workspace, <runDir>/tmp, <runDir>/home, :29-34); only the parent applies a winner. They are ephemeral, unregistered, non-resumable, pruned only by the same run.

[REUSE] In-process sub-work in llm-jev (DESIGN §22.2-22.3; LLM-JEV-DESIGN §4.8): `SynthesisContext.generate(req, {sample, purpose, signal})` fires N parallel samples per round (4/3/6 by class), each with its own AbortController linked to the step signal and a deadline; `cancel('commit'|'budget'|'abort')` closes a round and cancelled samples are metered at full estimate; `generator:start/delta/tool-delta/end` carry `sample`; `synth` events carry free-text phases (`llm:fire`, `llm:sample`, `llm:cancel`, ...). TUI streams sample 0 and shows k/N (src/tui/useEngine.tsx). The round cache is in-memory only (`synthState.llm` <= 4 KB index, bodies not persisted; a resumed step re-asks, ~$0.003).

[REUSE] Host-side control surface (types.ts:1545-1580 SessionHost; src/cli/session.ts): pause(), abort('human_abort'), steer/unsteer, retryNow, exit(code); the host holds exactly ONE `engine` variable; Ctrl-C => `engine.abort('human_abort')` (session.ts:3731), `exit(code)` with a live engine aborts first and exits after run:end (:3740-3748), SIGINT/SIGTERM => `engine.abort('signal', {signal})` (:4025); `Renderer.attach(engine)` is singular (types.ts ~1615). No multi-engine host, tab or child model exists.

[REUSE] Event/status vocabulary at main: EngineEvent (types.ts:1383-1437) has run:start/ready, step:*, stage:*, generator:* (with sample), synth, proposal, risk, confirm:*, exec:*, outcome, judge, plan, checkpoint, step:end, status, transcript, error, run:end {exitCode?, resumable?, paths?}, steer:*, pause:requested, budget:warn/stop/clamp/override/unpriced, retry/retry:settled, notice, workspace, blocking:request/resolved, secret-ack. EngineStatus (types.ts:1348-1373) has step/maxSteps/wallMs/stage/spend/stopReason/pausing/pendingDirectives/blocked/retrying/generatorTokens/jevCostBasis — no phase, subwork, pausePoint, context. StageName (types.ts:241) has no 'coordinate'; BlockingKind (:1161) no 'lease-conflict'; BlockingAnswer (:1162) no 'pause'|'wait'|'worktree'; InterruptReason (:393) no 'human_pause'; NoticeKind (:1376) no 'session'|'coordination'.

[DESIGN §3] Registry = file ledger `~/.jevcode/coordination/{registry,leases,inbox,acks,runs}/<deviceId>/…` plus device.json, repokeys/, trusted.json, ignored-devices.json, seen/<sessionId>.json, worktrees/<repoKey>/<slug>.json; single writer per subtree; no daemon. Heartbeat (<= 4 KiB, redacted, checksummed) every 15 s written at exactly six points (run:ready; the `.then` of the checkpoint IIFE; the 15 s timer; emitStatus phase/blocked/pausing/stage transitions coalesced 250 ms; finish(); the 'exit' handler synchronously) and carries `parentSessionId | parentRunId`, `phase: RunPhase`, `subwork[{kind:'sample'|'lane'|'probe'|'child', id, since, stage, detail60, laneDir?}] <= 16`, `spend.sessionUsd`, `declared/touched/touchedRecent`, `leases[]`, `pausePoint?`. Liveness: same device = phase !== 'ended' && pid alive && startedAt >= bootAt (beat age is display-only, 'hung?' after 45 s); other device = monotonic arrival age < ttl + slack (120 s shared-dir / 180 s git). `Ledger` is opened by the CALLER after renderer.firstFrame() and passed as `EngineOptions.coordination.ledger`, one per process; the engine never opens a second one; `peerLive(runId)` is a synchronous lookup over an already-folded ledger consulted by takeRunLock.

[DESIGN §4] Leases `{ type: 'intent'|'exclusive'|'command'|'lane'|'worktree'|'takeover', paths[] <= 64 (prefix-collapsed, truncated:true), laneDir? run-relative, slug?, stamp:{n,deviceId,runId}, expiresAt (10 min, renewed by the heartbeat timer), released?:{outcome:'committed'|'discarded'|'expired'|'ended', changed:{rel:sha256}} }`; claims default `advisory` (facts only: StepRecord.coord, a `notice kind:'coordination'`, a heads-up message, <= 8 x 200 chars into Jev risk state; p95 < 2 ms, zero file I/O on the step path), `strict` = awaited exclusive write + one readdir fence, inline wakeable wait <= 60 s, Jev Choice (proceed_now | wait_for_release | work_in_worktree | change_approach), then the `lease-conflict` pane `[w] wait [c] continue anyway [t] worktree [q] pause`. `coordination.enabled` defaults to `source !== 'bench'`; bench runs never coordinate, the bench PROCESS writes one `kind:'bench'` presence heartbeat and takes `bench.lock` O_EXCL (§4.7).

[DESIGN §5] Messages `{ id '<deviceId>-<actor8>-<seq>', from{deviceId,label,sessionId|null,runId|null,user}, to '<sessionId>'|'@<repoKey>'|'@all', type: heads-up|handoff|note|request-release|steer|pause|resume|end|abort|ack|who, text <= 600, refs{commit?,branch?,files?,leaseId?,runId?,step?,msgId?,target?}, by 'human'|'engine', expiresAt (7 d; control types 10 min) }`; acks one file per consuming SESSION; dedupe via seen/<sessionId>.json. Delivery: the TUI PROCESS is the recipient; `engine.deliver?(msg): AckOutcome` while a run is live; `steer` becomes a directive only from a trusted device (hmac, W5) else a `note`; `pause`/`end` apply without confirm only when the sender is this device or trusted with `remoteControl:'allow'`, else the `[y] at step end [Y] now [n] ignore` row (plain / --no-input: one line, ignored); `abort` ALWAYS the local `[y]`. Peer text reaches the generator only inside one fenced `## Other sessions` block after sanitizeStream. Automatic messages: heads-up on overlapping declare, `handoff` when the HEAD watcher sees a commit containing the run's files, `note` on run:end with uncommitted changes, a child's run:end => handoff to the parent session.

[DESIGN §6.1-6.4, 6.7] Sub-work joins the registry: `EngineStatus.subwork?` + heartbeat `subwork` derived from synth and generator:* events; lanes become `type:'lane'` leases through an ADDITIVE hook `SynthesisContext.coordination?: { laneClaimed(lane), laneReleased(lane) }` (types.ts ~1261) threaded into LaneContext and called after `git worktree add` (lanes.ts:214) and per lane in disposeLanes (:302-322) — so any later session can prune stale lanes of dead runs and a peer's `exclusiveTree` command gets a heads-up; round cache `<runDir>/cache/llm/<goalId>/<round>/<sample>.json` written ENGINE-side via new `store.writeCache(rel, json)` (<= 32 files LRU) with `LlmSourceDeps.replay?(goalId, round)` so a resumed step re-asks only missing samples; `CancelReason` gains 'pause'; pause-now aborts the shared controller, `LlmSource.cancel('pause')` closes the round, lanes get a `disposeSignal` (5 s) for resetLane/disposeLanes after the step signal aborted; finish() does NOT dispose lanes (pool lives in the synthesizer's mem).

[DESIGN §6.5] Child runs: `/spawn <task> [--own <globs>] [--worktree [slug]] [--mode m]` (or the strict `work_in_worktree` judgment) starts a CHILD RUN IN A NEW PROCESS — `jevcode run --parent <runId> --workspace ~/.jevcode/worktrees/<repoKey>/<slug> --plain --json` to a log, or `[f]oreground` as a second session tab — with its OWN sessionId (= its run id) and `parentSessionId` = this session, `parentRunId` = this run, `RunMeta.worktree = { slug, dir, branch, base }`. Recipe `git worktree add --lock --reason 'jevcode:<runId>:<sessionId>' -b jevcode/<slug> <dir> HEAD` (the git lock IS the marker; nothing untracked in-tree), metadata in `coordination/worktrees/<repoKey>/<slug>.json` with `syncedIgnored`, parent dirty set synced once (DIRTY_ENTRIES_MAX 200 rule). Depth capped at 1 (`coordination.childDepth`: a child cannot spawn); <= 3 live children per session (`coordination.maxChildren`). Child run:end sends a `handoff` (commit, or 'uncommitted on jevcode/<slug>') to the parent's inbox; parent TUI shows `child <slug> finished: 4 files on jevcode/<slug> — /merge <slug> · /diff <slug>`; `/merge <slug>` PROPOSES THE MERGE AS A TASK for the parent's next run (JevCode never runs a git write outside a judged step). Children receive `steer` only from the parent's device, open read-only in the TUI (<-/-> navigation), inherit the parent's sandbox profile, secretPaths and redactor, are their own runs for money (`/cost` shows `children: $x (2 runs)`). Leaving a TUI with live children => `children live: 2 — [k] keep running [e] end them [n] stay`; `[k]` keeps them under their own session ids. `run:start` index line gains `parentSessionId?`; picker indents children under the parent; `-c/--continue` never picks a child; the session spend meter folds child sessions into the parent's total (§14 Q9, W1 item 14). §6.6 sweep removes a session worktree only when locked with a `jevcode:` reason, no live heartbeat/lease references it, it is clean and merged (or no commits beyond base), and older than `worktreeRetentionDays` 30.

[DESIGN §7 / §12.0.2] Pause has one method and two moments: `Engine.pause(opts?: { at?: 'step'|'now'; by?: 'self'|'peer:<sid8>'|'device:<id8>' })` stays void. `at:'now'` (default chord `ctrl+x ctrl+p`, §14 Q1 unratified; `/pause now`) does, synchronously: (1) snapshot the draft to `cache/step-<n>.json` `{ step, stage, proposal, patchTargets, risk, matchesIntent, targets[{rel,sha256,bytes}], partial{text<=32 KiB}, llmRound{goalId,round,arrived[]}, directive, contextFiles }` via `persist(store.writeCache(...))`; (2) `pauseNow = pauseRequested = true`, emit pause:requested; (3) `controller.abort(new AbortError('human_pause'))` UNLESS `currentStage === 'execute'` (P4: WAIT, never kill — execute finishes, post-images taken, judge SKIPPED, step commits with `interruptedAt:{stage:'judge', reason:'human_pause'}`). Panes get a `blockWaker` so pause() resolves `{answer:'pause'}`. `abort()` after a pause-now records `abortOverride` so Esc Esc / SIGTERM still exit 130/143. `PausePoint { step, round, phase: StageName|'idle'|'pane', reason: 'step'|'now'|'now-after-execute'|'pane'|'worktree', resumableAt: 'boundary'|'cache/step-N.json', replayable, pane?, synthPhase?, by, end }` emitted as `pause:point` in finish() after the final state write and before run:end, also on the final `phase:'ended'` heartbeat. Table P1–P8 covers boundary, mid-stage, mid-LLM-round, mid-execute, mid-judge, pane open, lease-conflict [t], remote message. There is NO Engine.resume(): resume = `createEngine({ resume: { runId, force, replay } })` from the TUI's resumeRun after the §7.3 card (`[Enter] resume (fresh) [r] replay [f] fresh [d] diff [w] who`); replay verifies every target sha, ALWAYS re-runs risk and re-asks a review confirm. `Engine.end?(opts)` = pause + `RunMeta.ended {at, by}` + `session:end` index line + children asked to pause; createEngine refuses an ended run without --force. Idempotency: pause twice no-op; now after step UPGRADES; step after now no-op; end after pause sets end.

facts.ts FACT_KEYS/FACT_TOPICS/FACT_EXAMPLES/FACT_FALSE_EXAMPLES are closed tables and session.ts factsInput() feeds them — adding a 'memory' fact touches all four plus tests (test/unit/chat/facts.test.ts) and the intake question count.

WizardStep/WizardReason/WizardHost/WizardDetect/wizardLines/wizardRows/wizardConsoleTitle have no import step; the ≤ 4-row budget must be proven for the new step at 80x24, 40x8 and 12x60 (F-M, F-N, §1.8 row 8) and the found-row must truncate by cells (truncateCells) for long tool lists; tui-prompter.ts and plain-composer.ts need the twin prompts.

RunMeta/isRunMeta validate v1 fields only — `memory?`/`workflow?` must be optional and sessionFieldsOf/reindex must tolerate their absence; `workspace` event consumers (Transcript, plain.ts, json-stream) need the new field rendered as sizes/sha only.

workspace/files.ts listCandidates has no exclusion for `.jevcode/` — memory and workflow files would enter the 300-candidate prefilter and Jev's context Nouls and could be `read`/`edit`ed by the generator; an exclusion (like .git) plus a seatbelt `(deny file-write* (subpath <ws>/.jevcode/memory))` rule beside the .git/config denial (seatbelt.ts:110) is missing.

Non-interactive paths have no import behaviour defined: pipes, --no-input, --json, --mock, bench/perf sources must skip the step silently (one stderr line at most, like INSTRUCTIONS_NOT_TRUSTED_LINE) and never write files.
No .gitignore management exists — `.jevcode/memory/local/` needs a one-time `[setup]` hint or `jevcode memory init` that appends the ignore line after asking, never silently.

Codex's memories_1.sqlite, Claude/Codex session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl, ~/.codex/sessions) and Copilot's config carry private and possibly secret content with no public schema — explicitly out of scope; the onboarding copy must say what is NOT imported.

The Copilot page fetched lists no prompt-file (.github/prompts/*.prompt.md) format or size limits, and the Gemini page gives no import-depth limit — those two mappings rest on the other tools' conventions and should be marked 'best effort' in the dry-run output.
Windows: 0600/0700 cannot be enforced (credentials.ts P41 ACL note) — the same note must accompany ~/.jevcode/memory and imports/ writes; realpath/symlink rules need a Windows junction test.
hazards: Prompt injection: imported memories, rules, workflows and AGENTS.md are attacker-controlled text once a repo is cloned; they must stay generator-only (D6 — never in Jev state, never in the intake request), be rendered as fenced data under an explicit header, never execute (`!cmd`, ```! blocks, `hooks`, `allowed-tools` stripped with notices), never widen permissions or thresholds (risk 0.3/0.7 stay code constants), and every action they provoke still passes the risk stage.

Secret leakage: Claude auto-memory topic files and CLAUDE.local.md routinely hold sandbox URLs, tokens and credentials; import must refuse isSecretBasename/isMentionDenied paths, run detectSecrets on every body (exact + redacting families masked, warn-only families like AWS/PEM/JWT require an explicit y per file with the label only), never print a body in a `[setup]` item, `[ui]` row, index.jsonl (512-byte lines), history.jsonl, run.json or transcript.log — counts, paths and sha8 only; a throwing redactor must drop the entry (EREDACT pattern in history.ts), never store unredacted text.

Path escape via symlinks: a repo can ship `.jevcode/memory/x.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` or `.claude/rules/shared -> /etc`; reuse instructions.ts' realpath-inside-scope rule for every read, cap symlink depth, detect cycles, and treat any file resolving outside its source tree as skipped-with-notice (Claude's 'external import' approval is the precedent).

Trust bypass: project memory and workflows are untrusted workspace inputs exactly like AGENTS.md; if the trust gate is not extended, a `3 don't trust` decision would still load them; $HOME as a workspace must never persist a trust decision; a changed entry must re-prompt (digest), and `--trust-workspace` scripts must get the same one-line stderr behaviour.

Resource exhaustion: thousands of topic files, a 4 MiB CLAUDE.md, deep `@import` chains, circular symlinks, huge .mdc rules — bound the scan (files, bytes, depth, wall time), clip with recovery hints, keep the system prompt ≤ 32 KiB and the per-step slot ≤ 8 KiB so the generator prompt budget is not blown, and keep Jev's request byte-identical (D:990: no Jev request grows with the transcript or with memory).

Semantic loss on import: Claude `disable-model-invocation`/`context: fork`/`paths`, Cursor's four rule types, Copilot `applyTo`/`excludeAgent`, Codex override precedence and Gemini's concatenation order all mean different things; importing everything as flat 'always' text changes behaviour silently — require a dry-run table, per-field drop notices, default `always: false` for anything that had a scope, and mark best-effort mappings.

Duplicates and contradictions: the same AGENTS.md is read by Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and OpenCode and may also be imported by a CLAUDE.md `@AGENTS.md`; contradictory rules across tools; a project entry shadowing a user entry — dedupe by sha256, deterministic precedence user < project < local, record `source` so `/memory show` explains where a rule came from, and never import a file JevCode already reads through loadInstructions.

Staleness and wrong-project memory: auto-memory notes are branch- and time-specific ('northwind-2-1-branch-state'); Claude keys memory by git root slug, so importing another project's slug into this workspace is wrong — import only the slug matching this git root (offer others by name), stamp updatedAt/ttl, and provide `/memory prune`.

Self-modification: the workspace is writable inside the sandbox, so a run could rewrite `<ws>/.jevcode/memory` and poison its own future prompts; deny writes there like .git/config and .git/hooks, exclude it from listCandidates, and re-prompt trust when the digest changes between runs.

Write safety and reversibility: use writeFileAtomic (0600), never overwrite an existing entry without --force, write the manifest before the files so undo-import can always find what was written, verify sha256 before unlinking on undo, warn that imports appear as untracked files in a dirty git workspace, and ensure `.jevcode/memory/local/` is gitignored before writing personal preferences into a repo.

Onboarding regressions: a new step lengthens first run and can break pinned pty smokes (zero-arg-wizard, splash-*); it must be absent when nothing is found, one key to skip, never re-offered (bookkeeping row), keep Ctrl-C semantics (exit 2 only for a startup wizard with a missing key; a step with nothing missing must not print the fix block — §1.8 row 6), fit ≤ 4 rows at 40x8, and have --plain/--screen-reader/--ascii twins with tests, or it violates F1/F10 and the round-3 gates.

Workflow execution semantics: a workflow's `mode`/`budget` must use the pending-for-next-run rules of /mode and /budget (memory only; persistence only via `jevcode config set`) and remain under the session spend cap; `$ARGUMENTS` text must never be re-tokenised as a command or bypass the intake floor (a workflow starts a paid run only through the same submit path, with Jev's coding_task reading or an explicit user invocation); names must not collide with built-ins or aliases (D-K), and one-letter names are refused.

Concurrency and cross-device sync: two sessions importing simultaneously or a synced ~/.jevcode (COORDINATION-DESIGN single-writer rule) can tear INDEX.md — regenerate the index from files atomically (tmp + rename), never append, and treat a torn frontmatter as 'skipped with notice' rather than fatal.

Privacy of the inventory itself: even the detection row reveals which tools a user runs and how many projects they have; show counts only, keep the manifest 0600 under ~/.jevcode (seatbelt-unreadable), never log source paths at info level, and exclude imports/ from `jevcode report` bundles unless --include-imports.

topic: Reader 1 — prior art for multi-agent coding orchestration (Claude Code subagents/teams/worktrees/agent view/workflows + Agent SDK, Managed Agents multiagent, opencode, OpenHands SDK, Codex CLI, Devin CLI/cloud, Cursor/Jules/Copilot cloud agents, claude-squad/ccmanager/vibe-kanban/Gas Town, Magentic-One/MetaGPT/AgentCoder/MapCoder/HyperAgent, Anthropic engineering posts, Cognition's "Don't build multi-agents"): how each handles budgets, cancellation, pause/resume, isolation, merge/conflicts and UI control — mapped against <repo>/docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §6 (sub-agents/lanes/child runs), §7 (pause/resume/end), §11 (corner cases)
facts: CLAUDE CODE SUBAGENTS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents): defined as markdown+YAML in .claude/agents/ or ~/.claude/agents/; required fields name, description; optional tools, disallowedTools, model (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable|full id|inherit), permissionMode, maxTurns (output marked 'partial' at limit, v2.1.246+), skills, mcpServers, hooks (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop; Stop auto-converts to SubagentStop), memory (user|project|local), background, omitClaudeMd, effort, isolation: worktree, color, initialPrompt, experimental.cacheTtl. Combined descriptions >15,000 tokens warn at startup.

CLAUDE CODE SUBAGENT LIMITS: default nesting depth 3 below main (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH; 1 disables nesting); default 20 concurrent (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS; error 'Concurrent subagent limit reached'); ultracode sessions exempt; RESUMING a subagent takes a fresh slot without checking the limit; Agent tool withheld at depth limit (forks keep it but it errors). Restrict spawnable types with tools: Agent(worker, researcher). Empty tool set fails with 'Agent would be spawned with zero tools'.

CLAUDE CODE FOREGROUND vs BACKGROUND: interactive sessions default to fork mode ON (CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_MODE) so every subagent runs in the background; -p and Agent SDK default OFF (background by default but foreground when Claude needs the result; background:true forces background). Background subagents get a RESTRICTED tool set (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, PowerShell, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, Skill, ToolSearch, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, Monitor, TaskStop, SendMessage, Artifact, SubagentHandback + MCP); their permission prompts surface in the main session and a 'for the rest of the session' answer applies to the WHOLE session. Ctrl+B backgrounds a running task; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 forces foreground.

CLAUDE CODE SUBAGENT CONTROL: stop via 'x' on the row in /tasks or the subagent panel (row kept 30 s after stop/failure, removed immediately on success); Ctrl+X Ctrl+K (twice within 3 s) stops ALL background subagents; Esc denies one background permission prompt without stopping the subagent; stopped subagents never auto-resume; resume by SendMessage to the agentId/name (full history retained); built-in Explore/Plan are one-shot and return no agentId. Subagent output is scanned (v2.1.210+): harness control tags and Human:/Assistant: turn markers get a backslash inserted, a '[harness: ...]' marker line is prepended, nothing is removed.

CLAUDE CODE SUBAGENT ISOLATION/CONTEXT: non-fork subagents start fresh with own system prompt + task prompt + CLAUDE.md + git status snapshot + preloaded skills + sibling roster (v2.1.206+); no conversation history. Model resolution: per-invocation model > frontmatter model > CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL > main model (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 overrides first two). Context window is the subagent's model's, not the parent's. API error: foreground returns partial output with cut-off note; background marked failed with last output preserved.

CLAUDE CODE SUBAGENT WORKTREES (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees): isolation: worktree gives a temp worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ on branch worktree-<name>, branched from the REMOTE DEFAULT BRANCH ('fresh') unless worktree.baseRef='head'; auto-removed only if no changes; dirty ones kept until a periodic sweep older than cleanupPeriodDays that never removes worktrees with changed/untracked files or unpushed commits, or without Claude's git-metadata marker. Claude Code holds `git worktree lock` while the agent runs and releases stale locks from exited processes (v2.1.210+). Four enforcement checks block edits/commands/git redirects (git -C, --git-dir, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, cd) into the main checkout and refuse commands whose shape can't be verified. .worktreeinclude copies gitignored files (.env) into new worktrees. --worktree '#1234' branches from a PR head.

CLAUDE CODE WORKTREE SHARING/RESUME: worktrees share .git, project plugins, permission approvals (saved to main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json since v2.1.211) and read-through .claude/skills|agents|commands. Resume returns the session to its worktree after verifying it is a separate checkout; deleted worktree → resumes in launch dir and clears the binding; --fork-session starts in launch dir. stream-json result carries startup_failure_reason worktree_unverified | worktree_resume_refused (v2.1.274+).

CLAUDE CODE AGENT TEAMS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams, experimental, CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1): lead + teammates (separate full sessions, own context), shared task list (pending/in progress/completed, blockedBy dependencies, file-locked claiming, self-claim), mailbox JSON at ~/.claude/teams/{team}/inboxes/{agent}.json, team config ~/.claude/teams/session-<8 chars of session id>/config.json (removed at exit), tasks ~/.claude/tasks/{team}/ (persist for resume). Display modes teammateMode in-process | auto | tmux | iterm2 (--teammate-mode). Panel keys: ↑/↓ select, Enter view+message, Esc interrupts the viewed teammate's turn, x stops, Ctrl+T toggles task list; idle rows hide 30 s after whole panel idle; >3 idle collapse into 'N idle agents'. Hooks TeammateIdle / TaskCreated / TaskCompleted exit 2 = block + feedback.

CLAUDE CODE AGENT TEAM LIMITATIONS (verbatim list): no session resumption of in-process teammates (/resume, /rewind lose them; lead may message ghosts); task status can lag (teammates forget to mark completed, blocking dependents); shutdown slow (teammate finishes current request/tool call first; graceful shutdown request can be rejected with explanation); one team per session; no nested teams; no background subagents from in-process teammates (can't outlive lead); lead fixed; permission mode set at spawn (lead's mode, dontAsk not inherited; changeable per teammate later); split panes need tmux/iTerm2; teammates NOT worktree-isolated ('two teammates editing the same file leads to overwrites' → partition files). Lead auto-approves teammate plan approvals WITHOUT the user reviewing. /model and /fast apply to the lead only; /effort follows to teammates. Token cost ~7x a single session when teammates plan; advice 3–5 teammates, 5–6 tasks each.

CLAUDE CODE CROSS-SESSION MESSAGING (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging): ListAgents + SendMessage over a per-session Unix socket (/tmp/cc-socks-<uid>) or Windows named pipe; sessions register in files on disk; message is plain text with sender name + reply address; received Claude is told it came from another session — it cannot approve permissions, change config, or run slash commands; delivered between tool calls during a turn or starts a new turn when idle. Inbound control crossSessionInbound accept|hold|refuse; default holds when sender bypasses permissions and receiver prompts (or vice versa) behind an approval dialog with dialogExpiry (5 min). Caps: ~1M chars per message (refused at sender), bursts refused at sender, per-sender rate limit, identical repeats dropped, queue of 50, held cap 100, notify_when_idle one-shot expiring after 12 h. isolatePeerMachines=true requires approval for cross-machine sends even in bypassPermissions.

CLAUDE CODE AGENT VIEW / BACKGROUND SESSIONS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view, research preview): `claude agents` dashboard groups sessions Pinned / Ready for review (open PR) / Needs input / Working / Completed; states working | blocked | done | failed | stopped, status busy | waiting | idle, waitingFor 'permission prompt' | 'input needed' | 'sandbox request' | 'worker request'; Haiku-generated one-line summary refreshed ~15 s. Keys: Enter/→ attach, ← or Ctrl+Z detach (session keeps running), Space peek, Ctrl+X stop (again within 2 s deletes), Ctrl+T pin, Ctrl+R rename, Ctrl+S group by state/dir, Shift+↑/↓ reorder, Alt+1..9 attach by index. Dispatch: `claude --bg [--name] [--agent] [--model] [--exec]`, `/bg <prompt>`, `/fork <prompt>`, `claude --resume <id> --bg`. Shell: claude attach|logs|stop|kill|respawn|rm <id>, claude daemon status|stop --any, claude agents --json. Supervisor restarts crashed processes; idle unattached >1 h processes stop (conversation on disk); state in ~/.claude/jobs/<id>/state.json, ~/.claude/daemon.log. Background sessions auto-create worktrees before editing (worktree.bgIsolation='none' disables), commit+push a branch and open a DRAFT PR, never push main or force-push.

CLAUDE CODE DYNAMIC WORKFLOWS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows): a JS script (export const meta {name, description, phases?}; agent(prompt,{schema,label}), pipeline(items, fn), parallel([...]), phase(title), log(), `args` global) executed by a runtime outside the conversation; up to 16 concurrent agents (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS 1–256), 4,096 items per parallel()/pipeline(), 1,000 agents per run, 'Large workflow' warning at >25 agents or >1.5M projected tokens; no mid-run user input; Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() THROW inside the script so a relaunch repeats the same agent() calls. /workflows view keys: p pause/resume, x stop agent or whole run, r restart agent, s save as command, f filter. agent() resolves null when stopped or on unrecoverable API error. Fan-out siblings are held up to 5 s (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS) so they read the first agent's prompt cache.

CLAUDE CODE WORKFLOW RESUME SEMANTICS: relaunch replays agents in start order — completed agents return saved results; the FIRST agent whose prompt differs (edited script or upstream output changed) re-runs and so does every later agent; agents running when stopped start over; a FAILED agent (incl. one you stopped with x) re-runs and so does every agent started after it, even completed ones ('if A,B,C,D and B fails, A cached, B C D rerun'). Relaunch is refused while agents from the stopped run are still alive. Results persist under ~/.claude/projects/<session>/ and survive --resume and cloud VM reclaim; a missing result set fails with 'nothing to resume'. Usage-limit hits pause the run (agents wait for reset) up to twice, interactive+subscription only.

CLAUDE CODE TASK TOOLS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference): TaskCreate {title, status, blockedBy[], blocks[]}, TaskUpdate {task_id, status, title, details, blockedBy, blocks, delete}, TaskGet, TaskList; available by default only on Claude 3.x/Opus 4.0–4.7/Sonnet 4.0–4.6/Haiku 4.5, opt-in elsewhere via CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 or naming them in --allowedTools; not in -p, cloud, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry. CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID shares a list across sessions via ~/.claude/tasks/<id>/. TaskStop {id} stops a background task, teammate or named background agent (error lists running agents by id, v2.1.203+). Monitor runs a command/WebSocket and feeds lines back; subagent monitors stop when the subagent stops; timeout 5 min default / 30 min max. SubagentHandback (auto mode, v2.1.271+) delivers a subagent's report through the classifier.

CLAUDE CODE INTERACTIVE CONTROLS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode, /checkpointing, /sessions): Esc interrupts the turn (queued messages still send), Esc Esc on empty input opens /rewind (Restore code and conversation | Restore conversation | Restore code | Summarize from here | Summarize up to here), Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+X Ctrl+S interrupts and sends queued messages now, Up takes queued messages back, Ctrl+B backgrounds a Bash call, Ctrl+T toggles the task checklist. Checkpoints: one per prompt that starts a turn, 100 most recent kept, saved with the conversation so /rewind works after resume; NOT tracked: Bash edits, edits by any subagent except a foreground `context: fork` skill, external/concurrent-session edits, symlinked/hard-linked paths, directory create/move/delete. Resumed sessions restore conversation, model, agent, permission mode (terminal path only), active goal, unexpired scheduled tasks — but NOT background Bash/monitor tasks; a tool running at crash never finishes or re-runs. Two terminals resuming one session without forking interleave into one transcript. /branch keeps in-flight background subagents running (their output lands in the branch).

CLAUDE CODE /goal (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal): a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook; after each turn a small fast model (Haiku) returns Not yet met | Met | Impossible; several turns without tool use → loop stopped with warning; background work defers evaluation with check-ins at 30 min then doubling (cap 3 idle check-ins per goal, CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES); auth failure/credits exhausted/context overflow/model unavailable clear the goal; other errors retry ≤3 then pause; goal survives resume (turn count, timer, spend baseline reset). Condition ≤4,000 chars; users are told to embed 'or stop after 20 turns' as a bound.

CLAUDE AGENT SDK SUBAGENTS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents): `agents: { name: AgentDefinition }` with description, prompt, tools, disallowedTools (mcp__server, mcp__*), model, skills, memory, mcpServers, initialPrompt, maxTurns, background, omitClaudeMd (TS ≥0.3.271), effort, permissionMode; programmatic agents override filesystem ones; CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 removes general-purpose. Detect delegation via tool_use name 'Agent' (was 'Task' before v2.1.63) and parent_tool_use_id on nested messages. Resume: parse `agentId: <id>` from the Agent tool result text, pass resume: sessionId and the same agents map, mention the agent id in the prompt. Spend cap maxBudgetUsd / max_budget_usd counts subagent requests: at the cap spawning fails 'Budget limit reached', running background subagents are stopped, query ends error_max_budget_usd (Claude Code ≥2.1.217). TS `env` REPLACES the subprocess env (spread process.env); Python merges.

CLAUDE AGENT SDK LOOP/SESSIONS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop, /sessions, /typescript, /file-checkpointing): maxTurns counts tool-use turns only; result subtypes success | error_max_turns | error_max_budget_usd | error_during_execution | error_max_structured_output_retries; queued streaming input after max-turns starts a new turn with a fresh turn count but the budget keeps accumulating; /clear resets the budget. Query object: interrupt(), setPermissionMode(), setModel(), setMaxThinkingTokens(), streamInput(); options abortController, persistSession:false, resume, resumeSessionAt (message UUID), resumeDropsTurn (v2.1.223+), forkSession, continue, sessionStore (alpha) + loadTimeoutMs. Transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session>.jsonl (cross-directory lookup v2.1.223+). Read-only tools run concurrently, mutating tools (Edit/Write/Bash) sequentially; custom tools need readOnlyHint to parallelize. File checkpointing: enableFileCheckpointing + extraArgs {'replay-user-messages': null} → user message uuid = checkpoint; rewindFiles(uuid) requires an open connection (resume with empty prompt); skips links (skippedLinks); tracks Write/Edit/NotebookEdit only, same session only.

CLAUDE CODE HOOK EVENTS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): SubagentStart/SubagentStop (payload agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message, tool_use_count, cwd, permission_mode; matcher is unanchored regex), TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted (task_id, task_name), Stop (exit 2 keeps Claude working; payload last_assistant_message, tool_use_count, effort), PreCompact/PostCompact, SessionStart/SessionEnd, PermissionRequest (use decision object, exit 2 ignored), Elicitation (exit 2 blocks), WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove (replace git logic for other VCS). Settings/plugin hooks also run inside subagents with agent_id/agent_type. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} does not follow a worktree; the hook input `cwd` does.

CLAUDE CODE PARALLELISM COMPARISON (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents): five approaches — subagents (Claude delegates in one conversation), agent view (you dispatch independent sessions), agent teams (Claude plans/assigns/supervises peers), projects (cloud threads), dynamic workflows (a script holds the plan; 'Interruption: resumable in the same session' vs subagents/skills 'restarts the turn' vs teams 'teammates keep running'). Supporting tools: worktrees, cross-session messaging, /batch skill (5–30 worktree-isolated subagents each opening a PR). /tasks lists background shells + subagents; /workflows lists runs; `claude agents` lists background sessions. Headless: `claude -p` waits for background subagents/workflows up to CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS (10 min) then stops them and drops partial results; SIGTERM exits 143 leaving the turn unfinished (resume continues it), SIGINT/interrupt() ends the turn cleanly; --permission-prompts none denies anything that would prompt; --forward-subagent-text reconstructs nested subagent transcripts via parent_tool_use_id; system/init `capabilities` (e.g. interrupt_receipt_v1, interrupt_cancel_queued_v1) is for feature detection.

CLAUDE CODE COSTS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs): agent teams ~7x tokens when teammates plan; guidance: Sonnet for teammates, small teams, focused spawn prompts, shut teammates down when done (each active teammate keeps consuming tokens); subagent requests fall outside the main cache TTL bucket (5 min default; subagentPromptCacheTtl='1h' at higher write price); /usage attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers. Opus 5 'delegates to subagents more readily than prior models' — Anthropic recommends the instruction 'Delegate to a subagent only for large tasks that are genuinely independent and parallelizable… do not use subagents to verify or double-check your own work… keep spawn counts low' plus deterministic caps (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5#controlling-subagent-spawning).

ANTHROPIC MANAGED AGENTS MULTIAGENT (skill ref shared/managed-agents-multiagent.md; platform guide https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration.md): coordinator declares `multiagent: {type:'coordinator', agents:[id | {type:'agent',id,version} | {type:'self'} | {type:'advisor',model}]}`; 1–20 roster entries, ONE level of delegation (rostering an agent with its own roster fails validation), ≤25 concurrent threads (archive finished threads), threads share the container filesystem but not conversation; coordinator gets list_agents + send_to_agent; spawning returns immediately and the report arrives in a later turn; thread status running | idle | rescheduling | terminated; events session.thread_created/_status_running/_status_idle (with stop_reason)/_status_rescheduled/_status_terminated, agent.thread_message_sent/_received (direction relative to the stream's thread). Session status aggregates threads ('if any thread is running, session is running'); per-thread list_cost figures do not sum to the session total. Web-tool domain lists intersect (allow) / union (block) down the chain.

MANAGED AGENTS BUDGET + INTERRUPT SEMANTICS (skill refs shared/managed-agents-core.md § Session budgets, shared/managed-agents-client-patterns.md): budget `{type:'limit', max_list_cost:{amount,currency}}` is a hard, dollar cap enforced as a PRE-REQUEST gate — the request that crosses completes, so overshoot is at most one model request per running thread; at the cap the session goes idle with stop_reason budget_reached (not terminated; history + sandbox kept) and accepts ONLY settle events (user.tool_confirmation, user.tool_result, user.custom_tool_result, user.interrupt — the interrupt is accepted and ignored); no event resumes it, only changing/removing the budget (create-only; removal is one-way; new cap must exceed consumed cost); a thread at requires_action outranks budget_reached at session level; one shared budget across all threads. user.interrupt: 'the session keeps running until it reaches a safe boundary, then goes idle'. Correct idle gate: break only on idle with non-requires_action stop_reason or on terminated (idle is transient between parallel tools / awaiting confirmations); SSE emits status_idle slightly before the queryable status updates (post-idle race → 400 on archive/delete); reconnect must events.list() then dedupe by event id because SSE has no replay; processed_at null while queued.

OPENCODE AGENTS (https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/, https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/): primary agents (build, plan — plan sets edits/bash to 'ask') switched with Tab (agent_cycle / shift+tab reverse); subagents general (full tools), explore (read-only), scout (read-only external docs) invoked by @mention or the Task tool; config fields model, prompt (file), permission (allow|ask|deny, incl. task permissions controlling which subagents an agent may invoke), temperature, top_p, mode (primary|subagent|all), steps (max agentic iterations before forcing a text-only reply — its only cost control). JevCode's separate-process children (design §6.5) avoid the ghost problem only if the resume card marks children 'gone' and the parent inbox tolerates a handoff that never arrives (row 28).

Concurrency caps leak on resume: Claude Code's 'resuming takes a fresh slot without checking the concurrent limit' and Managed Agents' 'archive finished threads' rule show that resumed/parked children must count against coordination.maxChildren (3) and depth caps, or the cap is bypassable.

Permission laundering across agents: every surveyed system (Claude Code teams/cross-session, Managed Agents, Devin background 'unapproved tools automatically denied') treats another agent's message as untrusted and refuses relayed approvals; Claude Code additionally applies a background subagent's 'allow for the rest of the session' answer to the WHOLE session, and the lead auto-approves teammate PLANS with no user review. JevCode row 50 must keep child→parent messages as facts only and must not let a child's confirm answer widen the parent's rights (or vice versa).

Same-file edits without isolation overwrite: Claude Code agent teams are not worktree-isolated ('two teammates editing the same file leads to overwrites'); Cognition warns 'actions carry implicit decisions, and conflicting decisions carry bad results'. Default children to read-only/research (Devin subagent_explore, opencode explore, Codex explorer) or to disjoint path ownership + worktree; JevCode's lease `--own <globs>` and lane ownership rule (§6.3) are the equivalent guard.

Undo/rewind coverage holes: Claude Code checkpoints do not track Bash edits, subagent edits (except foreground forked skills), symlinks/hard links, or directory ops; SDK rewind needs an open connection. JevCode pre/post images must be per-worktree for children, and `/undo` after `/merge` must be a git revert, not an image restore.

Budget caps overshoot and gate semantics: Managed Agents' pre-request gate lets each running thread exceed the cap by one model request and rounds reported cost to the cent, then accepts only settle events; Agent SDK stops background subagents at maxBudgetUsd and refuses new spawns. A session spend cap that folds children (design §14 Q9) must expect N-children × one-request overshoot, define which events a capped child still accepts (pause/end/abort yes, steer no), and never rely on the displayed figure as the trigger.

Replay/relaunch semantics are subtle: Claude Code workflows re-run every agent after the first changed prompt or after a FAILED agent even if later agents completed, refuse relaunch while old agents are alive, and make Date.now()/Math.random() throw for determinism; Devin keys each agent call by hash(prompt, schema, settings). JevCode's sha-gated replay (§7.3 step 3) should also refuse to resume a parent whose child is still live (row 31 analogue) and key child results by (task, targets sha) so a changed upstream invalidates downstream children.

Stall and loop detection is mandatory for unattended children: Magentic-One re-plans after ≤2 stalls, Claude Code /goal halts after several tool-less turns and caps idle check-ins at 3, Gas Town flags GUPP violations, agent teams' leads 'stop early' or start implementing instead of waiting. Children need a no-progress timer (design §8.9) plus a parent-side 'child idle N min' fact and a wall-clock cap (Copilot 59 min, Devin workflow 7 d).

Task-state lag and stuck dependencies: Claude Code teammates 'sometimes fail to mark tasks as completed, which blocks dependent tasks' — any dependency graph (blockedBy) needs a manual override and a heartbeat-based staleness display, as in agent view's blocked/waitingFor states.

Shutdown is slow and leaves residue: teammates finish the current tool call before shutting down; killed background sessions leave `git worktree lock`s (Claude Code sweeps stale ones since v2.1.210); orphan tmux sessions persist; `claude -p` waits up to 10 min for background subagents then drops partial results. JevCode's 5 s shutdown bound (§7.5) must release child worktree locks by reason prefix and the sweep (§6.6) must prune half-registered worktrees.

Mailbox robustness: before v2.1.207 a single malformed inbox entry blocked delivery for that mailbox every second; Claude Code now validates and drops bad entries. Cross-session inbound defaults HOLD messages for 5 min (dialogExpiry) and drop them in -p sessions, cap held at 100, queue at 50, throttle loops and refuse bursts at the sender. JevCode row 25/26 already bounds inbox size; add expiry notices back to the sender so a parent never waits on a dropped handoff.

Pause vs interrupt semantics differ per system and users conflate them: OpenHands pause is read between steps (a running tool completes), Managed Agents interrupt drains to a 'safe boundary', Claude Code Esc interrupts the turn but SIGTERM leaves it unfinished (resume continues it) while SIGINT/interrupt() ends it cleanly, claude-squad 'pause' actually commits and deletes the worktree. JevCode's two-moment pause (at:'step' vs at:'now', execute never interrupted, row 29) needs the status line to say exactly which one is happening and what 'Esc Esc' would additionally destroy.

Worktree base-branch surprise: Claude Code branches new worktrees from the remote default branch ('fresh', with a 5 s fetch) unless worktree.baseRef='head', and reopening a clean merged worktree RESETS it to the default branch; subagent worktrees follow the same rule. JevCode branches from HEAD and syncs the dirty set (§6.5) — document this difference explicitly so users coming from Claude Code are not surprised, and never auto-reset a reopened worktree.

Token and cost multipliers: multi-agent research ~15x chat tokens, agent teams ~7x in plan mode, Opus 5 'delegates more readily' and over-verifies with subagents unless told not to. Cap depth (1), concurrency (3), and spend, and add Anthropic's delegation instruction to the generator prompt; the user's brief ('does not do a lot of mission-critical stuff but speeds up everything') matches read-only research children by default.

Foreground/background tool asymmetry: Claude Code background subagents lose AskUserQuestion, plan-mode tools, Workflow etc., and Devin background subagents auto-deny unapproved tools — a child that needs a human confirm must either be foreground or park at a pause point; JevCode children 'never receive steer from anyone but the parent's device' (§6.5) and must surface a `review`-class confirm to the parent TUI rather than silently auto-declining.

Session-view clutter and hidden state: agent panels hide idle rows after 30 s and collapse >3 idle into one row; hidden ≠ stopped, which confuses users ('teammates not appearing' troubleshooting). Any JevCode child row that is hidden must still be addressable and `sessions who` must list it.

Cross-directory and duplicate-copy resume: Claude Code resolves a session id across projects only when exactly one other project holds a transcript with messages, otherwise reports not-found; two devices resuming one run is JevCode row 31 (lower stamp wins, forked tail kept). Name collisions are renamed with a two-word suffix; JevCode uses label#id4 (row 42).

facts: CLAUDE.md hierarchy (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; project ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md; personal-uncommitted ./CLAUDE.local.md; managed CLAUDE.md via managed settings. Every CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md from cwd up to filesystem root loads at launch and is CONCATENATED root→cwd (closer = later = higher effective priority); CLAUDE.local.md is appended after its sibling CLAUDE.md. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load lazily when Claude reads files there. Block-level HTML comments are stripped. A file over 4 MiB is skipped; >200 lines is discouraged.

CLAUDE.md @imports: `@path` anywhere outside code spans/fences; relative to the CONTAINING file (not cwd); absolute and `@~/...` allowed; recursive to max depth 4 hops. An import in a project file resolving outside the working directory is an 'external import' that triggers a one-time approval dialog; the decision is stored per project in ~/.claude.json (observed keys projects[path].hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesApproved / hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesWarningShown). Real example on the reference machine: <workspace>/ProjectA/CLAUDE.md is exactly one line `@AGENTS.md`.

Claude Code rules: .claude/rules/**/*.md (recursive, symlinks allowed, circular detected) and user-level ~/.claude/rules/*.md (loaded before project rules). Optional YAML frontmatter `paths:` (list of globs, brace expansion, budget 1,000 expanded patterns / 4 MiB) makes a rule load only when matching files are read; rules without `paths` load at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md. Setting `claudeMdExcludes` (array of absolute-path globs, any settings layer) skips files.

Claude Code AGENTS.md (v2.1.277+): read directly ONLY when no CLAUDE.md/.claude/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists in cwd or any ancestor; ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, managed CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules do NOT count. Mode set via settings `pluginConfigs['agents-md@builtin'].options.instructionFiles` ∈ {claude-md-or-agents-md (default), claude-md-and-agents-md, claude-md, managed-only} (user/managed settings only). It never reads AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, or anything under .agents/. Claude's /init reads .cursor/rules, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md and (with CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1) AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/, .windsurfrules, .clinerules.

Claude Code auto memory (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#auto-memory): ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ (override: settings `autoMemoryDirectory` absolute or ~/ path; CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; disable via autoMemoryEnabled:false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1). MEMORY.md is an index, one line per memory, only first 200 lines or 25 KB loaded; topic files are read on demand. Docs list four `type` values: user, feedback, project, reference. Claude Code stamps `modified` (ISO 8601) into frontmatter on write. memory/ is EXCLUDED from the cleanupPeriodDays sweep (default 30 days) that deletes transcripts.

OBSERVED real memory format on the reference machine (43 topic files across 5 project slugs; bodies not read): every file has frontmatter `name:`, `description:` and a NESTED `metadata:` block containing `type:` (values seen: project 29, feedback 10, reference 4), plus in most files `node_type:`, `originSessionId:` (uuid) and `modified:` (ISO 8601). No file uses a flat top-level `type:` — so an importer must accept both flat `type` (docs) and `metadata.type` (actual). MEMORY.md index lines all match `- [Title](file.md) — summary`. Filenames are free-form slugs (feedback-*, project-*, <repo A>-*). Example dir: ~/.claude/projects/-home-dev-projects/memory/ (MEMORY.md 2 lines, feedback-max-parallel-agents.md, project-jevcode.md). A regex scan for key-like tokens across all 43 bodies matched 0 files.

Claude Code project slug = cwd absolute path with `/` replaced by `-` (observed: <workspace> → -home-dev-projects; a git worktree at JevCode/.claude/worktrees/llm-jev-int → -home-dev-projects-JevCode--claude-worktrees-llm-jev-int). Docs say auto memory is derived from the git repository so worktrees share one memory dir, but transcript slugs exist per worktree. IDEMPOTENCY AND CONSENT: Claude's own /import is 'one-time append'; re-running a naive importer duplicates content. Record an import manifest (source path, sha256, timestamp, destination) in JevCode config, skip unchanged sources, offer dry-run/diff and per-item picker (matching Claude's `/import --dry-run` / `--yes` UX), and treat any agent- or script-supplied 'approval' as non-authoritative — only the user's own TUI confirmation may write.
